frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes EGRESS: the passage of an entity from within a bounding/containing locus to the outside of it — a boundary-crossing whose determinate direction is interior→exterior ("coming, or being brought, to be outside of what previously held it"). The root supplies only the out-directed transition plus the implied prior enclosure/source; whether the entity moves of itself, is driven out by an agent, or is procured out is a matter of FORM (I intransitive egress; IV causative "bring/drive/produce out"; X "extract, draw out"), and what the enclosure is (womb, earth, home, grave, darkness, concealment, a container) is a matter of CONTEXT.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes EGRESS: the passage of an entity from within a bounding/containing locus to the outside of it — a boundary-crossing whose determinate direction is interior→exterior ("coming, or being brought, to be outside of what previously held it"). The root supplies only the out-directed transition plus the implied prior enclosure/source; whether the entity moves of itself, is driven out by an agent, or is procured out is a matter of FORM (I intransitive egress; IV causative "bring/drive/produce out"; X "extract, draw out"), and what the enclosure is (womb, earth, home, grave, darkness, concealment, a container) is a matter of CONTEXT.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across every form-family the same "out-of-an-interior" vector recurs. Form I (V) is the entity itself crossing out: kharaja minhaa "he went out of it" (28:21); takhruju min afwaahihim, words "come out of their mouths" (18:5); yakhruju min butuunihaa sharaab, drink "comes out of their bellies" (16:69); yakhruju min bayni s-sulb (86:7, semen); yakhrujuuna mina l-ajdaath, they "come out of the graves" (70:43); kharajuu min diyaarihim (2:243, 8:47). Form IV (V(IV)) is the causative — an agent effects that same egress of an object: akhrajakum min butuuni ummahaatikum "brought you out of your mothers' wombs" (16:78); fa-akhraja bihi mina th-thamaraat "brought forth fruits by it [water]" (2:22, 14:32, 6:99, 7:57); yukhriju l-hayya mina l-mayyit "brings the living out of the dead" (6:95, 10:31, 30:19, 3:27); akhrijuuhum min qaryatikum "drive them out of your town" (7:82, 27:56); yukhrijuhum mina z-zulumaati ila n-nuur "brings them out of darkness into light" (2:257, 5:16, 14:1, 33:43, 57:9, 65:11). Form X (V(X)) profiles procuring/effecting the egress = extract: istakhrajahaa min wiʿaaʾi akhiihi "drew it out of his brother's bag" (12:76); tastakhrijuu minhu hilyah "extract ornaments from it" (16:14, 35:12); yastakhrijaa kanzahumaa "bring out their treasure" (18:82). The nominals nominalize the same event: khuruuj / yawmu l-khuruuj "the coming-forth" (50:42, 40:11, 9:46, 9:83); makhraj "a way out" (65:2) and makhraja sidqin "a true bringing-out" (17:80); ikhraaj "the driving-out/expulsion" (2:217, 2:240, 2:85, 9:13, 60:9); active participles mukhrij "one who brings out" (2:72, 6:95, 9:64) and passive mukhraj/mukhrajuun "one(s) brought out" (15:48, 23:35, 26:167, 27:67, 71:18); and the go-forth-participle khaarijiin "coming out" (2:167, 5:37, 6:122). Even the abstract senses stay inside the same interior→exterior frame: yukhriju l-khabʾ "brings out the hidden" (27:25), mukhrijun maa taktumuun / maa tahdharuun "brings out [into the open] what you conceal/dread" (2:72, 9:64), yukhrij adghaanahum "brings out their [hidden] rancor" (47:29, 47:37) — all "the concealed interior brought to the exterior."
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtract (a) FORM: Form I = subject undergoes the egress (intransitive "go/come out"); Form IV = agent causes the object's egress ("bring out, expel, produce, make manifest"); Form X = agent seeks/effects the egress ("extract, draw out"); verbal nouns (khuruuj, ikhraaj) = the egress-event as such; makhraj = the locus/manner of egress; participles mukhrij (agent) / mukhraj/khaarij (undergoer). Subtract (b) CONSTRUCTION: min + NP marks the source-interior left behind (min butuun, min diyaar, min al-ajdaath, mina z-zulumaat) — near-ubiquitous; ilaa + NP optionally marks the destination (ilaa n-nuur); ʿalaa + people = "go forth toward/upon" (kharaja ʿalaa qawmihi 19:11, 28:79); bi- instrumental in production ("bring forth by means of water"); the direction OUT is supplied by the root, not by these particles. Subtract (c) PARTICIPANTS: God, prophets, tyrants, the earth, plants, semen, water, words, the dead — the mover/producer varies freely. Subtract (d) CONTEXT: creation/provision, cosmic sign, expulsion-from-homes polemic, Exodus/magicians narrative, marital law (65:1), tribute (18:94), resurrection eschatology. What remains invariant after all four subtractions is the bare interior→exterior transition — egress.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The nominal kharj / kharaaj "tribute, levy, yield" (18:94:13:1 "shall we assign you a kharj?"; 23:72:3:1 and 23:72:4:2 "do you ask them a kharj? — but the kharaaj of your Lord is better"). On the surface this is a payment/return, not a spatial exit. It reconciles as the nominalization of the productive branch of egress: kharaaj is "that which is issued/rendered forth" — a yield or outlay brought out from a source. The bridge is internally attested in this very packet, where God's repeatedly "brings forth" (akhraja) provision, fruit, grain and pasture out of the earth (2:22, 6:99, 7:57, 79:31, 87:4); 23:72 explicitly contrasts a human-demanded kharj with "the kharaaj of your Lord [who] is the best of providers" — i.e., the divinely-issued-forth provision. So kharj/kharaaj = the thing rendered/produced-out, which keeps the interior→exterior residue at the nominal level. It is the single occurrence-set where the residue is not surface-spatial and needs this nominalizing bridge.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is "SEPARATION / REMOVAL from a place" (loss of location). It covers expulsion (min diyaarihim) and exiting well, but it is arbitrated against by the internal data: (i) it fails the productive/emergence cases — bringing forth fruit, grain, pasture, a shoot (48:29), the living from the dead — which are creation/issuance, not mere removal; (ii) it does not capture the determinate OUT direction that the antonym pairings force. A second alternative, "MANIFESTATION / appearance," covers 27:25 and 47:29 but under-covers the massive physical-expulsion and exiting material (you are not made to "appear" from your home). Egress is the only candidate that is the literal base of both the physical (exit/expel) and the derived (produce, extract, make-manifest) clusters, with the latter reachable by an internally-attested bridge (the concealed interior brought to the exterior), whereas the reverse derivations do not work. Internal evidence therefore arbitrates for egress over both.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbor is dxl "enter" (دخل), the exact polar antonym; the data pairs them repeatedly and thereby fixes xrj's direction as OUT: adkhilnii mudkhala sidqin wa-akhrijnii makhraja sidqin (17:80), tuuliju … wa-tukhriju (3:27), maa yaliju fi l-ard wa-maa yakhruju minhaa (34:2, 57:4). It is also distinct from the vertical-motion roots nzl "descend/send down" and ʿrj "ascend," which stand beside xrj in 34:2/57:4 (yalij/yakhruj vs. yanzil/yaʿruj) — xrj is emergence-out-of a locus, not up/down. It differs from nbt "sprout/grow" (intrinsic growth) in that xrj of plants profiles their emergence OUT of the earth by an external producer (yakhruju nabaatuhu, 7:58; akhraja shatʾahu, 48:29), and from zhr/brz ("become manifest / come into the open") in that xrj requires a bounded source-interior that is crossed, not mere visibility. Falsifiability: the unity breaks if any confirmed occurrence denotes entering, remaining inside, or a motion with no interior→exterior transition (or a direction toward an interior). No such occurrence exists in the 182.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — interior→exterior egress — is recoverable in all 182 occurrences, and its direction is determinate everywhere, reinforced by explicit antonymic pairing with dxl "enter" (17:80, 3:27, 34:2, 57:4), which no rival meaning explains. Form I gives the bare intransitive egress, Form IV the causative bring/drive/produce-out, Form X the procured extraction, and the nominals the event/locus/participants of the same transition; the abundant min-source construction (min butuun, min diyaar, min al-ajdaath, mina z-zulumaat) makes the source-interior explicit again and again. The derived senses — "make manifest" (27:25, 47:29, 2:72, 9:64) and "produce/yield" (fruit, grain, pasture, 2:22, 6:99, 79:31, 87:4) — are reached by a bridge internally attested in the same corpus (the concealed or latent interior content brought out to the exterior), not imported. The only place the residue is not surface-spatial is the noun kharj/kharaaj "tribute/yield" (18:94, 23:72), and even there it is the nominalized "that which is rendered/issued forth," anchored by 23:72's own contrast with God's provision that He brings forth. No occurrence stays unreconciled, so inconsistent_refs is empty and clean universal presence holds; I judge STRONG because the residue is surface-recoverable across the entire verbal system and all major nominals with a sharply distinct, determinate direction, the single tribute-noun set being a well-bridged nominal rather than a counterexample.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial sweep over all 182 occurrences. The EGRESS core (interior->exterior boundary-crossing, min-source enclosure, direction fixed OUT, self-motion vs causative vs procure-out = FORM) fits the entire verbal inventory (I/IV/X) and the event/participle nominals (khuruuj, makhraj, ikhraaj, mukhrij/mukhraj, khaarijiin) with no strain: exit from homes/graves/wombs/darkness/earth, expulsion, extraction, production of provision/plants, words from mouths, semen, pearls, hidden things made manifest. Hardest cases attacked: (1) the tribute/levy/yield nominals 18:94:13:1 (kharjan), 23:72:3:1 (kharjan), 23:72:4:2 (kharaaju) - the ONLY occurrences denoting a thing/amount rather than a transition, the natural seam for a homonymy split. They resolve, not by ad-hoc rescue but by a principled, independently-attested metonymy internal to this root: kharaaj = 'what comes out of the land' (yield/produce), kharj = 'what is paid out'; and the root elsewhere explicitly fuses provision with egress (akhraja...rizqan 2:22, akhraja bihi mina th-thamaraat 14:32). So khaaraaju rabbik = 'what God brings forth is better' sits squarely inside the vector as product-of-egress, covered by the candidate's own IV 'produce out'/nominalization clause. By the task's own criterion (failure = saveable only by circular/ad-hoc reasoning) these do NOT qualify - the derivation is legitimate and attested. (2) Abstract 'bring out the concealed' (27:25, 2:72, 9:64, 47:29, 47:37, 79:29 brightness, 3:110 nation brought forth) all instantiate concealed-interior->manifest-exterior. Neighbor-root contrast: sharply distinct from antonym dxl (exterior->interior), from nzl/Erj (vertical, source above, no enclosure), and from brz (emerge into prominence/open, which profiles becoming-manifest rather than exit-from-a-container); xrj's diagnostic is the obligatory min-source enclosure the neighbors lack. Falsifiable: a non-directional, interior-directed, or source-less sense would break it; none exists. No genuine failing occurrence survives - unity is distinct and falsifiable.
